2026-09-07T12:39:32.2133321Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2133826Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2134247Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2134900Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2135413Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2136093Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2138480Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2140942Z >
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2144231Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2147878Z >
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2148942Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2150012Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2150237Z ### How to Use
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2150539Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2151476Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2152454Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2152678Z ```bash
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2153357Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2154329Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2155137Z ```
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2155401Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2155723Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2156426Z ```bash
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2157126Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2158363Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2159499Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2160514Z ```
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2160777Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2161629Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2162821Z ```bash
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2163549Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2164469Z ```
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2164727Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2165126Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2166024Z ```bash
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2166728Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2168074Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2169008Z ```
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2169257Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2169603Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2170169Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2172183Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2174460Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2174686Z ```bash
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2175247Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2176389Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2177652Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2178077Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2178693Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2180086Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2181182Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2181786Z ```
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2182038Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2183087Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2184385Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2184601Z ```bash
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2185473Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2186680Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2187789Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2188368Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2188919Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2190013Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2190731Z ```
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2190989Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2191249Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2192318Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2193650Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2194971Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2196354Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2197929Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2198669Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2198891Z ### Notes
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2199161Z 
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2200034Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2202001Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2203807Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2205554Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2207193Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2208908Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2210257Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-07T12:39:32.2211199Z </mcp-clis>
